sentences.text: The Third and Fourth Respondents have filed Counter Affidavit stating that they have inspected the hotel premises of the Seventh Respondent and issued notice under Section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act' for brevity), on 20.05.2019 to the Seventh Respondent requiring him to obtain license to run the said hotel, apart from pointing out to rectify certain other irregularities, which have been identified.

3. It is further contended that the Fourth Respondent has once again inspected the premises of the Seventh Respondent on 09.08.2019 and has found that neither the defects pointed out earlier were rectified nor the Seventh Respondent had applied for license to run the hotel.
In such circumstances, it was recommended for the closure of the hotel http://www.judis.nic.in3/6 under Section 31 of the Act, until proper and valid license was obtained.
The Seventh Respondent has also given a written undertaking stating that he will not run the hotel without valid licence.
A photograph has been produced before this Court showing that the said hotel has been closed.
Nothing remains for further consideration in the matter.
4. Recording the aforesaid subsequent events, the Writ Petition is disposed.

It is also made clear that if the Seventh Respondent re-commences business without licence or rectifying the defects, it is open to the Petitioner to seek necessary redressal before the proper forum in that regard.
No costs.
